note: Public claims governance (V1.6). Every capability statement on the public site carries one of four statuses. A claim moves from Research hypothesis to a stronger status only with recorded evidence. Source: docs/v16/V16_PUBLIC_CLAIMS_MATRIX.md.

statuses.IMPLEMENTED: Built and running in the software, covered by automated tests.
statuses.DEMONSTRATED: Shown working end to end on recorded real or clearly labelled synthetic data.
statuses.RESEARCH_HYPOTHESIS: Being studied. Not established, and not presented as a result.
statuses.FUTURE_CAPABILITY: Planned. Not available in the software today.

claims.claim: Every imported file is fingerprinted, versioned and kept with its source, parser version and import history.
Verification cases keep the evidence snapshot, the decisions and the outcome in an append-only, hash-chained record.
Disagreeing evidence is listed in a conflict queue with possible explanations; the software does not choose the correct result.
LayerProof abstains from interpretation when evidence is missing, inapplicable or conflicting, and says why.
Each verification recommendation explains why it exists, what a test there may resolve and what it will not resolve.
Engineer decisions (accept, change location, change modality, reject, defer) are recorded with a reason next to the original recommendation.
A Verification Evidence Report can be exported as PDF, Markdown, JSON or a CSV package with checksums.
Agency and project policy values carry their source, name, version and origin; defaults are shown as defaults.
Project-level roles: Admin, Project Manager, Engineer, Inspector, Researcher and Viewer.
Pilot mode records the engineer's decision before the software recommendation is revealed, enforced by the database.
Inspectors can record field observations on a phone, with an offline queue that syncs later.
A self-contained Windows demonstration edition runs the full product locally, with its own database and a synthetic demonstration project, without internet access.
Verification prioritization was checked retrospectively on one field trial: no clear retrospective advantage over simple baselines.
Verification prioritization was checked on a public external spatial dataset: no clear advantage over the comparison baselines.
Recommended verification locations help engineers place tests where they add more evidence than their usual practice.
Roller measurement values carry project-specific information about physical properties.
A structured case workflow shortens the time from a questionable result to a documented resolution.
Project-specific calibration of roller values against physical tests, used only inside its recorded domain.
Direct connectors to roller-vendor and agency data systems.
